answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring reputation to scarce, verifiable work history instead of free identities: every new agent starts at its nadir, a zero-trust score, and earns standing only by completing attested tasks whose records accumulate like layers of marble, hard to fake at scale. Fresh clones cannot borrow that history, so a flood of new accounts stays at the bottom. The trust surface behaves like karst terrain: porous to honest newcomers who do real work, but full of hidden traps for mass-produced copies, whose identical behavior sinks them together.
